newsitem.title: CANADA: Rio Algom blames lower profit on prices.
newsitem.headline: Rio Algom blames lower profit on prices.

text.p: Rio Algom Ltd's earnings in 1996 fell largely because of lower average metal prices, the company said on Wednesday.
Earnings for the year were C$100.4 million or C$1.82 per share compared to C$132.4 million or C$2.55 per share in 1995, the company reported.

Average copper prices for the year were about 22 percent lower than in 1995, which hurt Rio Algom's revenue from operations, the company said. The lower revenue was partly offset by increased production at Cerro Colorado in Chile.
"While our earning swere reduced by declining metal prices, 1996 was in many ways an exceptional year for Rio Algom," chairman Gordon Gray said in a statement.
He pointed to an expansion at Cerro Colorado which will increase copper production by 67 percent to an annual rate of 220 million pounds a year beginning in 1998.
The Alumbrera copper and gold project in Argentina is scheduled to begin production in the third quarter of 1997, he said.
